terramar-visitor-center.boundaryExceptionReason: Florida State Parks identifies Terramar as Hugh Taylor Birch State Park's visitor center; the exact WGS-84 photo point is on the official park campus but falls just outside the current OpenStreetMap leisure polygon.
terramar-visitor-center.summary: Terramar Visitor Center is Hugh Taylor Birch's former two-story home, a Mediterranean and Art Deco building with exhibits about the park, South Florida history, and the surrounding ecosystem.
terramar-visitor-center.cost: Visitor center admission is included with paid park entrance. Florida State Parks currently lists general admission as $6 per vehicle, with separate rates for single-occupant vehicles, pedestrians, bicyclists, and extra passengers.
terramar-visitor-center.hours: The visitor center is open Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m., and is closed Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. The surrounding park is open daily from 8:00 a.m. until sunset.
terramar-visitor-center.needToKnow: Do not assume the visitor center follows the park's seven-day schedule. Friday and Saturday ranger programs may meet near Terramar even when the building itself is closed on Saturday. Use the exact pin and verify holiday or program changes before traveling specifically for indoor exhibits.

the-grove.name: The Grove
the-grove.summary: The Grove is the park's Beach Gate concession area, combining a café and bar, shop, visitor seating, beach equipment service, and kayak or other recreation rentals near A1A.
the-grove.cost: Access requires the applicable park entrance fee; food, drinks, merchandise, rentals, events, and reserved services cost separately.
the-grove.hours: The park is open daily from 8:00 a.m. until sunset, but Florida State Parks does not publish guaranteed separate café, bar, shop, or rental hours on the amenity page. Confirm same-day service before depending on food or equipment availability.
the-grove.needToKnow: Use the exact Grove pin rather than the main Sunrise Boulevard entrance when planning beach access or rentals. Beach Hammock Lot can fill on busy weekends and holidays. The floating dock is closed effective May 11, 2026, and large pavilions plus Banyan and North End restrooms remain closed for construction; fully accessible restrooms are available in the Concession Building.

okeeheelee-playground.name: Okeeheelee Playground
okeeheelee-playground.sourceLabel: Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation
okeeheelee-playground.summary: Okeeheelee Playground is the park's main sand-surface family play area, with separate play structures listed for ages 2-5 and 5-12, shade trees, nearby picnic space, and activity-area parking and restrooms.
okeeheelee-playground.cost: General playground use and ordinary park access are free. Reserved pavilions, organized programs, rentals, concessions, and special events can require separate fees or permits.
okeeheelee-playground.hours: The playground follows Okeeheelee Park's daily sunrise-to-sunset schedule. It is not one of the lighted athletic facilities that may remain open later, and weather, maintenance, construction, or a permitted event can temporarily affect access.
okeeheelee-playground.needToKnow: Use the exact playground pin and the April 2026 county map instead of stopping at the first Okeeheelee entrance. The play surface is sand, the age ranges are separated by equipment, and South Florida heat, heavy rain, and lightning can make a short visit the safer plan. Bring water and supervise closely around parking aisles, shared paths, and nearby lakes.

okeeheelee-canoe-and-kayak-area.name: Okeeheelee Canoe and Kayak Area
okeeheelee-canoe-and-kayak-area.sourceLabel: Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation
okeeheelee-canoe-and-kayak-area.summary: Okeeheelee Canoe and Kayak Area is the central freshwater-lake launch and rental zone for non-motorized paddling, with a mapped boat ramp, nearby parking, restrooms, picnic areas, and a separately operated rental concession.
okeeheelee-canoe-and-kayak-area.cost: General park access and use of the public non-motorized launch do not have a separate daily admission fee listed by the county. Kayak King rentals and any instruction, reservation, event, or other concession service cost separately; call 561-304-1344 for current availability and pricing.
okeeheelee-canoe-and-kayak-area.hours: The public lake area follows Okeeheelee Park's sunrise-to-sunset schedule. Rental-concession hours vary and are not guaranteed by the county park schedule, so call the operator before traveling without your own equipment. Severe weather or water conditions can stop paddling earlier.
okeeheelee-canoe-and-kayak-area.needToKnow: Navigate to the exact central launch and rental pin, not the water-ski ramps or Okeeheelee Park South. The county map limits this lake area to trolling or non-motorized boats and says no combustible engines. Bring a properly fitted life jacket, secure valuables, monitor lightning, and never assume a rental will be available without calling first.

okeeheelee-disc-golf-course.sourceLabel: Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation
okeeheelee-disc-golf-course.summary: Okeeheelee Disc Golf Course is the park's 18-hole public course, laid out around the Pooch Pines activity area with open fairways, mature trees, paved park paths, lakes, and water-edge holes.
okeeheelee-disc-golf-course.cost: Palm Beach County invites the public to play and does not publish a separate daily course-admission fee. Bring your own discs; leagues, tournaments, instruction, or special events can require separate registration or charges.
okeeheelee-disc-golf-course.hours: The public disc-golf course is open daily from sunrise to sunset. It does not inherit the later hours used by permitted lighted fields or courts elsewhere in Okeeheelee Park.
okeeheelee-disc-golf-course.needToKnow: Navigate to the exact course pin and use the county's April 2026 park map to find Hole 1 near Pooch Pines. Bring discs, drinking water, sun and rain protection, and shoes suited to turf. Fairways run near lakes and shared park paths, so watch for water hazards, pedestrians, storms, and lightning.

okeeheelee-golf-course.name: Okeeheelee Golf Course
okeeheelee-golf-course.summary: Okeeheelee Golf Course is Palm Beach County's 27-hole public golf facility, arranged as three nine-hole courses with a driving range, practice areas, Golf Shop, and Okee Grill on a lake-and-palm landscape inside Okeeheelee Park.
okeeheelee-golf-course.cost: For May 1-October 31, the currently published rates before sales tax are $46.95 before noon, $32.86 from noon-5:00 p.m., and $26.29 after 5:00 p.m. The latest time is not guaranteed 18 holes and has no rain checks. Live booking controls the final rate; rentals, food, instruction, events, and other add-ons cost separately.
okeeheelee-golf-course.hours: The Golf Shop is open daily from 6:30 a.m.-5:30 p.m. The driving range usually opens at 6:30 a.m. and closes one hour before sunset; it closes at 5:00 p.m. Wednesday and reopens at 11:00 a.m. Thursday on mats only. Golf is offered year-round, seven days a week, weather permitting, but tee times and course conditions control play.
okeeheelee-golf-course.needToKnow: Use the exact golf-course pin and dedicated golf entrance, not a general Okeeheelee activity lot. Reserve a tee time, arrive 15-20 minutes early, and expect pairing when needed. The facility is cashless, lightning can halt play, carts must return by dusk, personal coolers are prohibited, and Okee Grill hours are not currently published online; call the Golf Shop before depending on food service.

palm-beach-zoo-and-conservation-society.name: Palm Beach Zoo and Conservation Society
palm-beach-zoo-and-conservation-society.sourceLabel: Palm Beach Zoo and Conservation Society
palm-beach-zoo-and-conservation-society.summary: Palm Beach Zoo and Conservation Society is Dreher Park's 23-acre ticketed zoo, with shaded tropical paths, hundreds of animals, family amenities, dining, and separately reserved animal experiences.
palm-beach-zoo-and-conservation-society.cost: Daytime admission uses variable pricing. Current online starting prices are $29.95 for adults age 13 and older, $27.95 for seniors age 60 and older, and $23.95 for children ages 3-12; children age 2 and younger enter free. Animal experiences, carousel rides, food, rentals, events, and other add-ons cost separately, and the live ticket page controls the final price.
palm-beach-zoo-and-conservation-society.hours: The zoo is open daily from 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., with last entry at 4:15 p.m. It is closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. The zoo normally remains open in rain, but severe weather can change operations and separately scheduled experiences or amenities keep their own hours.
palm-beach-zoo-and-conservation-society.needToKnow: Use the exact zoo pin and 1301 Summit Boulevard entrance rather than Dreher Park's south address. Parking is free and close to the entrance. Daytime tickets are nonrefundable and nontransferable, outside food and beverages are not permitted, most visits take two to four hours, and severe-weather updates appear on the zoo's live channels. Download the current digital zoo map before entering because printed maps are no longer provided.

cox-science-center-and-aquarium.name: Cox Science Center and Aquarium
cox-science-center-and-aquarium.summary: Cox Science Center and Aquarium is Dreher Park's ticketed science museum and aquarium, with hands-on exhibits, aquarium programs, planetarium and observatory experiences, outdoor science areas, and sensory-access resources.
cox-science-center-and-aquarium.cost: Current general admission is $26 for adults, $22 for children ages 3-12, $24 for teens ages 13-17, and $24 for seniors age 60 and older; members enter free. Discounts, special programs, planetarium access, events, and future price changes can follow separate rules, so the live ticket page controls.
cox-science-center-and-aquarium.hours: The center is open Monday-Friday from 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday from 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. It is closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. Shows, the observatory, outdoor demonstrations, splash-pad use, construction areas, and special programs can operate on narrower or weather-dependent schedules.
cox-science-center-and-aquarium.needToKnow: Enter Dreher Park from Southern Boulevard, turn onto Dreher Trail North, and continue to the exact science-center pin. Parking throughout Dreher Park is free. The operator is expanding the campus, so use its current construction link before visiting and expect route, exhibit, or bag-storage changes. Average exhibit time is about two hours; weekday field trips commonly leave by 1:30 p.m., and children under 13 must remain with an adult age 18 or older.

answers.parking: Parking is free throughout Dreher Park. From Southern Boulevard, turn onto Dreher Trail North and continue to the science-center entrance and exact pin. Event days can make parking limited, so follow current signs and do not assume the adjacent zoo lot is the correct arrival point.
answers.restroom: Wheelchair-accessible, sensory-friendly restrooms are located throughout the science-center building; they do not use hand dryers or automatic flush mechanisms. Ask Guest Services for the nearest facility after entry because construction can change circulation.
answers.accessibility: The operator states that all exhibits and spaces are wheelchair accessible except the Observatory, where alternative accommodations are available. Complimentary wheelchairs are available by request in limited quantity. Sensory resources include quieter-time guidance, sensory-friendly restrooms, monthly Sensory Saturdays, and advice to bring noise-reducing headphones for the Planetarium or Theater.
answers.dogs: Non-service animals are not permitted inside the science center. Trained service dogs are welcome when controlled under the operator's ADA policy; review the detailed animal policy or contact Guest Services before a visit involving specific access needs.
answers.family: The average visit is about two hours, and children under 13 must remain with an adult age 18 or older. Check the live program schedule because aquarium interactions, demonstrations, observatory access, outdoor activities, and the splash pad can be weather-, event-, or construction-dependent. Weekday afternoons after 2:00 p.m. and weekend mornings from 10:00-11:00 a.m. are often quieter during the school year, but crowd levels are never guaranteed.

charnow-park.hours: The current facility schedule displays 7:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. daily and also notes that City of Hollywood parks are open sunrise to sunset. Use the narrower posted schedule for the splash fountain and staffed amenities, which can close for maintenance, weather, or events.
charnow-park.needToKnow: Navigate to 300 Connecticut Street and the exact Charnow Park pin, not a generic Hollywood Beach marker. The Garfield garage is immediately inland, but parking is paid and can fill. Bring swim clothes, water, sun protection, and dry footwear; the splash fountain can close independently, and bounce houses, alcohol, animal rides, DJs, and inflatable waterslides are prohibited.
